subject: UNLOCK statement
notes: RULE (two halves): 'Any record locks associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1 are released by the execution of the UNLOCK statement. The presence or absence of any record locks does not affect the success of the execution of the UNLOCK statement.' - cite.py --check 14.9.47.4 (first sentence) -> OK §14.9.47.4 1). CODE: FileRegistry.Unlock calls `PhysicalFileTable.ReleaseAllForConnector(st, name)` - keyed on the CONNECTOR name, which is exactly 'associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1' - then unconditionally `c.SetStatus(FileStatusCode.Success)`, so held locks and no locks give the same 00. The RECORD/RECORDS word is deliberately dropped (`_ = records;`), which is right: GR1 releases ALL locks and its NOTE routes single-record release to READ ... NO LOCK. BOTH HALVES MEASURED. (a) release: conformance:cases/9.1.13.9-File-sharing-conflict-condition-with-unsuccessful/file_sharing has A lock record 1 (READA=00), B blocked (READB=51), then `UNLOCK F-A` and B reads 00 (AFTER=00); file_sharing_seq shows the converse - B's UNLOCK does not disturb A's own lock (UNLB=00 then REWA=00; B's next REWRITE, after its UNLOCK and not a READ, is REWBU43=43, GR5 before GR11). (b) presence-or-absence: p1.cob UNLOCKs an OPEN sequential file that never held a lock -> 00, and p6.cob UNLOCKs twice in a row (AUTO-UNLA=00 then AUTO-UNLA2=00 with nothing left to release). (c) ALL LOCK MODES, not just MANUAL: p6.cob uses `LOCK MODE IS AUTOMATIC` on two RELATIVE connectors - the auto-lock taken by A's READ blocks B (AUTO-READB=51) and is released by `UNLOCK F-A` (AUTO-READB2=00), matching Table A.1's UNLOCK row, cite.py --check D.2.4.3.2 '| UNLOCK | Automatic -single - multiple Manual - single - multiple | | for all lock modes: - on all locked records |' -> OK (informative corroboration; GR1 is the normative source). NOT DOWNGRADED by the unregistered-connector path of findings [unregistered-keyed-connector]/[unlock-registry-entry-is-the-one-silent-fall-through]: a connector that was never registered was never opened, so it holds no record locks and GR1 is vacuous there - the observable failure on that path is the I-O status, which is why GR2 and GR3 carry it and this row does not.
